credential_request.title: Asks for OTP, PIN or password
credential_request.explanation: The message asks you to share or enter a secret such as an OTP, PIN, CVV or password. Banks and UPI apps never ask for these.
credential_request.tip: Anyone asking for your OTP or PIN is trying to take money out, not put it in.
advice: Never share OTP, PIN, CVV or passwords with anyone.

suspicious_link.title: Suspicious link
suspicious_link.explanation: The link does not look like an official website.
suspicious_link.tip: Banks and universities do not send shortened or look-alike links. Type the official address yourself.
advice: Do not click the link. Open the official app or type the official website yourself.

urgency_threat.title: Creates urgency
urgency_threat.explanation: The message pushes you to act fast so you do not stop and think.
urgency_threat.tip: Real organisations give you time. Pressure to act 'now' is a classic scam trick.
advice: Slow down. Do not act on a deadline set by a message.

account_threat.title: Threatens your account
account_threat.explanation: The message says your account, card or KYC will be blocked or suspended to scare you into acting.
account_threat.tip: If you are worried about your account, check it in the official app, not through the message.
advice: Check your account status only in the official app or by calling the number on your card.

prize_bait.title: Prize, refund or cashback bait
prize_bait.explanation: The message promises a prize, refund, cashback or reward you did not expect.
prize_bait.tip: If you did not enter a contest or ask for a refund, the 'reward' is bait.
advice: Ignore unexpected prizes or refunds. Real refunds go back to your account automatically.

payment_pressure.title: Pay to receive money
payment_pressure.explanation: The message asks you to pay, approve a request or enter your PIN in order to 'receive' money. You never need to pay or enter a PIN to receive money.
payment_pressure.tip: Entering your UPI PIN always sends money out. It is never needed to receive money.
advice: Do not approve collect requests or enter your UPI PIN to receive money.

sender_mismatch.title: Sender does not match
sender_mismatch.explanation: The message claims to be from an organisation, but it was sent from a personal number or an unrelated address.
sender_mismatch.tip: Banks send SMS from short codes like 'VM-SBIINB', not personal mobile numbers or Gmail addresses.
advice: Check the sender. Official messages do not come from personal numbers or free email.

brand_impersonation.title: Uses a trusted name
brand_impersonation.explanation: The message uses the name of a bank, payment app, university or government body together with other warning signs.
brand_impersonation.tip: Scammers borrow trusted names. The name alone proves nothing.
advice: Contact the organisation through its official app or website, not through this message.

generic_greeting.title: Generic greeting
generic_greeting.explanation: The message starts with 'Dear customer' or similar and asks you to act. Your real bank knows your name.
generic_greeting.tip: A generic greeting plus a link or request is a common phishing pattern.

link_checks.shortener: It is a shortened link, which hides the real destination.
link_checks.raw_ip: It points to a raw IP address instead of a website name.
link_checks.not_https: It does not use a secure (https) connection.
link_checks.odd_tld: It ends in an unusual domain ending often used by scam sites.
link_checks.lookalike: The website name looks like an imitation of a real one (extra hyphens or words like 'kyc' or 'login').

Low: Low risk signals found, but this is not a guarantee.
When in doubt, don't pay or share.
Medium: Verify through the official app or the number on your card, not the contact details in this message.
High: Do not reply, click, pay or share anything.
If you already shared details or paid, call your bank immediately.
